points.text: Dot-and-cross diagram for $\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$: $\text{H} \overset{\circ}{_{\times}}\text{N}\overset{\circ}{_{\times}}\text{H}$ with $\times\times$ lone pair above N and $\overset{\times}{\text{O}}$ / $\text{H}$ below N
M2: Oxidation numbers: N in $\text{NO}_2$ is (+)4, N in $\text{HNO}_3$ is (+)5, N in $\text{NO}$ is (+)2
points.guidance: 3 correct oxidation numbers – 2 marks; 2 correct oxidation numbers – 1 mark

points.text: M1: Nitrogen / N (in nitrogen dioxide) is both gaining electrons and losing electrons during the reaction
points.guidance: relates the term disproportionation to the reaction described

points.text: M2: Refer to relevant transfer of electrons when $\text{NO}_2$ reacts to form $\text{HNO}_3$ and $\text{NO}$: $\text{NO}_2$ to $\text{HNO}_3$ involves loss of electron(s) AND $\text{NO}_2$ to $\text{NO}$ involves gain of electron(s)
M1: State the effect of $\text{NO}$ gas on contact with moist air: $\text{NO}$ reacts with water OR $\text{NO}$ reacts with oxygen and water
M2: Consequence of M1 in terms of atmospheric pollution: causing acid rain OR photochemical smog / ground level ozone OR destroy ozone layer
